archetypes.name: commit-guard-collision
archetypes.rationale: The plan adds a new fixup commit and mixes git add -u (Option A) vs git add -A (Option B) — collisions with existing commit-pattern matchers and untracked-file invariants deserve a dedicated check.
archetypes.prompt_body: Examine whether the planned fixup commit subject ('chore: pre-rebase working-tree fixup (#3209)') could accidentally match any commit-inspection regex beyond the two acknowledged in the plan (the bump and changelog matchers). Search drop-bump-commit.sh, drop-changelog-commit.sh, any history-scanning scripts, and bump-version logic for additional subject-pattern guards that might mis-classify or skip the fixup commit. Then check the git add scope inconsistency: Option A uses 'git add -u' (tracked-only) while Option B uses 'git add -A' (all files including untracked) — verify whether 'git add -A' in Option B could accidentally commit new untracked files that the issue description explicitly excludes from the stall scenario and that Guard 1 explicitly ignores via --untracked-files=no. Also verify that the --untracked-files=no guard in the re-check condition is applied consistently between the two options and that neither option changes the effective scope of what 'dirty tree' means to downstream callers. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: line-target-accuracy
archetypes.rationale: The plan cites many specific line numbers and function anchors in ship-pr.sh, review-and-fix.sh, and drop-bump-commit.sh; if any have drifted the implementation lands in the wrong location.
archetypes.prompt_body: The plan references specific line numbers and code shapes: drop-bump-commit.sh Guard 1 at lines 85–94; ship-pr.sh run_rebase_rebump at lines ~2842–2873, the refresh-run-logs pre-flush at ~2851, the drop-bump-commit.sh invocation at ~2858, the CI-fix shape at lines 1806–1813, and the DROPPED=false stall block at lines 2865–2875; review-and-fix.sh apply_findings_with_coder commit_sha set at ~460 and success result block at ~464. Read each of these files and verify that the cited line numbers correspond to the described code: function boundaries, guard conditions, and surrounding context. A mismatch means the implementation inserts the new guard or follow-up commit in the wrong position, potentially breaking adjacent logic or silently missing the fix site. Also verify that the 'round_num > 0' scope guard the plan describes in review-and-fix.sh is the actual branch variable and condition used in the file — not a renamed or differently-typed variable. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
